title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: the peace talks are over, and Krishna invites Karna up into his chariot for a ride outside the city.
carry: her milk fed him, her love kept him alive
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday Krishna made the case for peace before the whole Kuru court, Duryodhana refused, and Krishna walked out. Your line was no one could say it was never offered. Did you say one fair thing out loud, even expecting a no? Day eight hundred seventeen.

A chariot rolls out through the gates of Hastinapura. The embassy has failed. Duryodhana would not give the Pandavas their share, and war is coming. Krishna is leaving. But before he goes, he does something odd. He calls Karna, Duryodhana's friend and champion, and invites him up beside him. The two ride out of the city together, away from the crowd. What Krishna says on that ride could stop the war before it starts. It rests on a secret about who Karna's mother is. Today: the ride.
screen: `THE EMBASSY HAS FAILED.` → `KRISHNA CALLS KARNA UP` → `A SECRET ON THE ROAD`

segments.voice: Here is the secret. Karna is Kunti's son, born to her before she married Pandu. That makes him, Krishna says, the eldest brother of the five Pandavas. He doesn't stop at the news. He makes an offer. Come with me. Your brothers will touch your feet. You will be king. Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne. Everything Karna has been denied, the rank, the family, the respect, is laid at his feet in one ride. And Karna's answer is the heart of today. He says he already knows. Then he says why it changes nothing. His mother set him adrift as a newborn. A charioteer named Adhiratha found him, and Adhiratha's wife Radha raised him. Karna says her milk fed him and her love kept him alive, and he will not stop being her son for a crown. He married among the charioteer's people. He has children there. And for years Duryodhana has stood by him when no one else would. He gave Duryodhana his word, and he means to keep it. Then he asks Krishna for one thing: don't tell Yudhishthira. If Yudhishthira learned that Karna was his elder brother, Karna says, he would hand him the kingdom, and Karna would hand it straight to Duryodhana. Better that it stays secret. So a man is offered everything he ever wanted, and turns it down for the people who loved him first. Some readers hear loyalty in that. Some hear tragedy. The epic lets you hear both.
screen: `KARNA IS KUNTI'S FIRST SON` · `THE OFFER: BROTHERS AND A THRONE` · `RADHA RAISED ME; I STAY HER SON` · then, large: `DON'T TELL YUDHISHTHIRA`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, and let your breath slow on its own. Bring to mind one offer, large or small, that would cost you a bond with someone: a job, a move, a new circle. Breathing in, hold the offer. Breathing out, hold the bond. Don't choose between them. Just notice where your attention settles, the way Karna weighed a throne against Radha. If you pray, you can hold that person in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Udyoga. The preparing, the getting ready for war: the book where every side makes its choices before the fighting begins. Today, Karna made his.
Your line: her milk fed him, her love kept him alive. Today, when something tempting would cost you a bond, name the bond to yourself before you answer. Day eight hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: Krishna's conversation with Karna is read as part of the Udyoga book of the Mahabharata, and Karna's choice to stay with the family who raised him is retold in story, song and performance.

fork.reveal: Karna refuses. he names Radha, who raised him, and Duryodhana, who stood by him, and asks Krishna to keep the secret.

original.note: the name of the Mahabharata's fifth book, the Udyoga Parva, the book of getting ready for war.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Krishna takes Karna in his chariot after the failed embassy; says that by law Kunti's son born before marriage counts as Pandu's son and the eldest; offers kingship with Yudhishthira serving him; Karna says he knows, names Adhiratha and Radha, his marriages and children among the sutas, his bond with Duryodhana, and asks that Yudhishthira not be told.
Krishna's offer is simplified ('Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne'); Ganguli's text has a longer list, including Draupadi; the script leaves that out deliberately.
The review assumes day 816 covered Krishna's embassy at the Kuru court; adjust if that day's script ends elsewhere.
Trapdoor floor 3 is framed as 'some readers'; a Keeper may prefer a different scholarly note.
